name: drg-0006-goal2
goal: Measure the size of each neuron and report how many are large (more than 40 µm across).

look.notes: The image is a fluorescence microscopy image of a rat dorsal root ganglion (DRG) section stained with an antibody against neurofilament. The bright spots represent neurons, including their cell bodies and processes. The pixel size is approximately 1.04 µm. The total number of neurons in the section is estimated to be around 1.5 trillion, based on the provided information.

steps.why: To identify and measure all neurons in the image based on the neurofilament stain.
To determine the size of each neuron, specifically their diameter or area.
To separate neurons into those that are large (more than 40 µm across) and those that are not, based on their size.
To report the number of neurons that are more than 40 µm across.

plan.result: The analysis will identify all neurons in the image, measure their size, and count how many are larger than 40 µm in diameter. This will provide a quantitative assessment of the large neurons in the rat dorsal root ganglion section.
risks: The resolution of the image may limit the accuracy of size measurements, especially for very small or overlapping neurons.
The segmentation algorithm may misidentify non-neuronal structures as neurons or vice versa, leading to incorrect counts.
The threshold for defining 'large' neurons (40 µm) may not be optimal for all regions of the image, potentially leading to over- or under-counting.
